title: Aphelion frame grid, selected view, and publish checkpoint
content:
Aphelion continued from a working live image wall into a more deliberate framed browsing surface. This pass focused on keeping the center image clean, moving interaction state into the surrounding block field, tightening the page frame, and making the server/publish flow match the new runtime requirements.

What changed:

  • Framed image stage: the hover preview is now a centered 640px square with a persistent light-gray border and no drop shadow.
  • Four-zone block field: the grid calculator now reserves the center square and lays blocks only in the top, bottom, left, and right zones around it.
  • Persistent selection marks: clicked blocks can be toggled light blue and saved in browser storage so a visitor can return to what they touched.
  • Selected view: when highlights exist, Aphelion shows Selected and Clear. Selected opens a minimal page with Back and a responsive image grid that defaults to four columns, drops to two on smaller windows, and expands to five on wide displays.
  • Page frame: Aphelion now has matched top/bottom banners, side gutters, and light-gray frame lines around the block field.
  • Server image sizing: the backend now serves centered 1024px square JPEGs through /api/image instead of sending the original full-size files.
  • Production runtime cleanup: the server script now starts with node dist/server.cjs, Vite is dev-only, and sharp is installed as the image resizing dependency.
  • Publishing polish: dummyaphelion is bundled into the build, and the Aphelion publish helper now sends the frontend to ASO while also syncing runtime files, including dist, to the server folder.

Feed also received individual post permalinks and Share buttons beside entry dates, so entries can now be linked directly with URLs like /feed/#entry-123.

This checkpoint makes Aphelion feel much more like a real framed viewing instrument: the image sits still in the center, the touched blocks live around it, and the backend now sends a smaller square image format better matched to the interface.
